transcript.text: gas hob keeps clickin on its own since i cleand it, stops then starts agen. drivin me mad. pls help

This is usually moisture or cleaning residue around a burner cap or the white spark electrode, rather than a gas-supply fault. It can make the ignition system click intermittently after cleaning. 1. Turn every burner control fully off. If the clicking is continuous, isolate the hob at its electrical switch/fused spur while you clean it.
2. When the hob is cool, lift off each burner cap and its metal crown. Dry them thoroughly, including underneath; kitchen roll followed by leaving them off to air-dry for a while is useful.
3. Gently wipe around the white ceramic spark electrode beside each burner. Do not force or bend it, and do not spray cleaner directly onto it.
4. Put each crown and cap back exactly flat and centred. A cap sitting slightly crooked can cause ignition trouble. If the clicking stops after drying and re-seating, that was the cause. If it continues after everything has had plenty of time to dry, particularly if it clicks with all knobs off, moisture may have reached an ignition switch or the spark module; that needs a Gas Safe engineer rather than dismantling the hob yourself. If you smell gas at any point, turn the controls off, ventilate the room, avoid switches/flames, and contact the gas emergency service on 0800 111 999.
ok did all that. i sloshed loads of water around when cleaning and one cap was wonky, fixed it. unplugged the hob under the sink all afternoon and its stopped clicking. no gas smell btw

That points strongly to water around the ignition area, with the wonky cap also contributing. As it has stopped after drying out and re-seating the cap, it should be fine to use normally. For next time, avoid flooding around the burner controls/electrodes and use a damp cloth rather than pouring water on the hob; then leave the caps off briefly to dry before refitting them flat. If the clicking returns when everything is dry and all knobs are off, isolate it electrically and arrange a Gas Safe engineer, as moisture may have got into an ignition switch. Is there anything else with the hob you’d like help with?

candidates: Moisture, grease or a burner cap not seated correctly after cleaning (high)
Moisture affecting an ignition electrode or ignition switch (medium)
Ignition switch or spark module fault (low)
